newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 13.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Thursday:

WASHINGTON - Four planned receptions for wealthy Democratic financial benefactors to mingle with President Clinton at the White House have been scrapped in recent weeks out of concern they would only deepen the political damage from the ongoing furor over campaign money.
WASHINGTON - President Clinton has abandoned the idea of establishing an independent panel to reduce the cost-of-living adjustments for Social Security and other federal benefits.
WASHINGTON - President Clinton plans to nominate Eric Holder, the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, to become the number two official at the Justice Department.
WASHINGTON - The aging bus system that takes 2,390 children with disabilities to and from school is broken, according to District of Columbia school officials.
GOMA, Zaire - Zaire's rebel leadership is sprinkled with veterans of the '60s uprisings when revolutionaries had their dreams of conquest crushed at a city called Stanleyville.

WASHINGTON - After two years of recommending the bare-minimum county school funding needed to qualify for state aid, Montgomery County Executive Douglas Duncan will propose to spend substantially more in his new budget.
WASHINGTON - Sanya Tyler, coach of Howard University's triumphant women's basketball squad, takes her team into the NCAA tournament.
